amendments.summary: The overall rationale for the changes implemented in the amendment is to • add new AESI of "malnutrition and inadequate fluid intake" and update the title and text for AESI of "ketoacidosis due to inadequate nutritional intake and other types of metabolic acidosis and ketosis" • provide more detailed guidance on recommending, monitoring, and managing nutritional intake and hydration • update criteria for dose modification, and • include adjudication of urgent visit for heart failure.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Minimum age requirement
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Participant must be at least 18 years of age or the legal age of consent in the jurisdiction in which the study is taking place at the time of signing the informed consent, whichever is older.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Type 2 diabetes diagnosis
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Have a clinical diagnosis of T2D based on the World Health Organization classification or other locally applicable diagnostic standards (see Section 10.8).

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: HbA1c range at screening
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Have HbA1c ≥7.0% (53 mmol/mol) to ≤9.5% (80 mmol/mol) despite diet and exercise treatment, as determined by the central laboratory at Visit 1 (screening).

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Insulin and antihyperglycemic medication naivety
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Are naïve to insulin therapy except for gestational diabetes or ≤14 days use for acute treatment and have not used any oral or injectable antihyperglycemic medications during the 90 days preceding Visit 1, or between Visit 1 and Visit 3 (randomization).

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Motivation and ability to follow study procedures
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Are motivated and willing to make themselves available for the duration of the study and are able to follow study procedures as required, including: store provided study intervention as directed; perform SMBG per protocol; maintain a study eDiary; complete patient questionnaires; and self-inject study intervention. Note: Persons with physical limitations who are not able to perform the injections must have the assistance of an individual trained to inject the intervention.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Stable weight prior to screening
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Are of stable weight (self-reported change ≤5 kg or 11 pounds) for at least 90 days prior to Visit 1 and agree to not initiate an intensive diet or exercise program during the study with the intent of reducing body weight other than the lifestyle and/or dietary measures for diabetes treatment.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Minimum BMI requirement
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Have a BMI ≥23.0 kg/m2 at Visit 1.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Sex and contraceptive/barrier requirements
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Males, WOCBP, or WNOCBP may participate in this trial. Contraceptive use by participants should be consistent with local regulations regarding the methods of contraception for those participating in clinical studies. For the contraception requirements of this protocol, see Section 10.4. Note: the word "male" is used to describe an individual assigned male at birth (AMAB) and the word "female" is used to describe an individual assigned female at birth (AFAB), for simplicity.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Informed consent capability
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Are capable of giving signed informed consent as described in Section 10.1.3, which includes compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the ICF and in this protocol.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Type 1 diabetes exclusion
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Have T1D.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: History of ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar state
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Have a history of ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar state or coma within the last 6 months prior to Visit 1, or between Visit 1 and Visit 3.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: History of severe hypoglycemia or hypoglycemia unawareness
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Have a history of severe hypoglycemia or hypoglycemia unawareness within the last 6 months prior to Visit 1, or between Visit 1 and Visit 3.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Current or planned treatment for diabetic retinopathy and/or macular edema
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Are currently receiving or planning to receive treatment for diabetic retinopathy and/or macular edema, for example, laser photocoagulation or intravitreal injections of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor inhibitors. Note: All participants will have a baseline fundus photography assessment. In the presence of any degree of diabetic retinopathy and/or macular edema, further ophthalmologic assessment will follow local standards of care to confirm eligibility.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Prior or planned surgical treatment for obesity
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Have a prior or planned surgical treatment for obesity. Exceptions: The following are allowed if they occurred >1 year before screening (Visit 1): liposuction; cryolipolysis; or abdominoplasty.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Prior or planned endoscopic or device-based therapy for obesity
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Have a prior or planned endoscopic (for example, mucosal ablation or gastric artery embolization) and/or device-based (for example, lap band, intragastric balloon, or endoluminal duodenal-jejunal bypass liner) therapy for obesity. Exception: Prior device-based therapy is acceptable if device removal was more than 6 months prior to screening (Visit 1).

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: NYHA Class IV congestive heart failure
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Have New York Heart Association Functional Classification IV congestive heart failure.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Recent cardiovascular conditions
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Have had any of the following CV conditions within 90 days prior to Visit 1, or between Visit 1 and Visit 3: acute myocardial infarction; cerebrovascular accident (stroke); or hospitalization for congestive heart failure.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Gastric emptying abnormality or drugs affecting GI motility
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Have a known clinically significant gastric emptying abnormality, for example, severe diabetic gastroparesis or gastric outlet obstruction, or chronically take drugs that directly affect GI motility.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Hepatic conditions or abnormal liver laboratory values
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Have acute or chronic hepatitis, including a history of autoimmune hepatitis, signs or symptoms of any other liver disease other than MASLD, or any of the following as determined by the central laboratory during screening: ALT or AST level >5.0× ULN for the reference range; ALP level ≥1.5× ULN for the reference range; TBL level ≥1.5× ULN for the reference range, except for cases of known Gilbert's syndrome; hepatitis B infection, defined as positive hepatitis B core antibody and positive for HBV DNA, or positive hepatitis B surface antigen; and positive hepatitis C antibody and positive for HCV RNA.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Severely reduced eGFR
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Have an eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m2 as determined by the central laboratory at Visit 1 (calculated by Chronic Kidney Disease-Epidemiology cystatin-c equation).

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Clinically relevant hematological condition interfering with HbA1c
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Have any clinically relevant hematological condition that may interfere with HbA1c measurement, for example, hemolytic anemias or sickle cell disease.

estimands.name: Primary Efficacy Estimand - Treatment Regimen Estimand (HbA1c Change from Baseline) - Retatrutide 4 mg vs Placebo
estimands.populationSummary: Adult participants with Type 2 Diabetes and inadequate glycemic control with diet and exercise alone, naive to insulin therapy (except gestational diabetes or ≤14 days acute use), and not treated with any oral or injectable antihyperglycemic medications within 90 days prior to study entry, with HbA1c ≥7.0% to ≤9.5% (Intent-to-Treat (ITT) Population) Summary measure: Difference in least squares means of change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 40.

intercurrentEvents.name: Treatment discontinuation (Primary Efficacy Estimand - Treatment Regimen Estimand (HbA1c Change from Baseline) - Retatrutide 4 mg vs Placebo)
intercurrentEvents.text: Permanent discontinuation of study intervention before Week 40. Under the treatment regimen estimand, treatment adherence is part of the treatment condition; all data regardless of discontinuation are included.

intercurrentEvents.name: Initiation of additional antihyperglycemic medications (Primary Efficacy Estimand - Treatment Regimen Estimand (HbA1c Change from Baseline) - Retatrutide 4 mg vs Placebo)
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant initiates additional antihyperglycemic medications (rescue therapy) during the study. Under the treatment regimen estimand, this is considered part of the treatment condition; all data are used regardless of initiation.

intercurrentEvents.name: Dose modification or interruption (Primary Efficacy Estimand - Treatment Regimen Estimand (HbA1c Change from Baseline) - Retatrutide 4 mg vs Placebo)
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant undergoes dose modification or temporary interruption of study intervention. Considered part of the treatment condition and not an intercurrent event.

intercurrentEvents.name: Permanent discontinuation of study intervention
intercurrentEvents.text: Participant permanently discontinues study intervention before Week 40. Handled using the hypothetical strategy: the outcome is estimated as if the participant had remained on their randomly assigned study intervention for the full 40 weeks.

The SoA described below should be followed for all participants enrolled in Study J1I-MC-GZBY (GZBY). However, for those participants whose participation in this study is affected by exceptional circumstances, such as pandemics or natural disasters, please refer to Section 10.14 for additional guidance.
Visit procedures may be conducted over more than 1 day if all activities are completed within the allowed visit tolerance period of each visit.

On all fasting visits, study participants are required to report to the site in a fasting condition, after at least 8 hours without eating, drinking (except water), or performing any significant physical activity. Additionally, the participant should not take their study intervention before the fasting visit. If a participant is adversely affected by the fasting condition, they are allowed to eat; however, specific study procedures need to be completed while fasting.
If a participant attends a fasting visit in the non-fasting state, reschedule the visit at a time within the allowable visit interval.

Visit 2 may occur as soon as the criteria for Visit 1 are confirmed. At Visit 2, screening laboratory results will be reviewed to confirm eligibility. Visit 3 to occur no sooner than 18 days after Visit 1.
The only procedure performed for these visits is PK sample collection.
For early discontinuation that occurs before the last visit in treatment period, see the activities listed for ED in the SoA.

A posttreatment safety follow-up visit will occur approximately 4 weeks following the last treatment period visit. Participants who have discontinued study intervention early and are only willing to come back for Visit 11 (Week 40) are not required to complete a safety follow-up visit if they have been off of study intervention for at least 28 days (see Section 7.1.1).
Unscheduled visits may occur as needed.

Monitor closely and routinely assess the need to adjust or discontinue antihypertensive medications, diuretics, laxatives, and anti-emetics. Refer to Sections 6.9.1 and 10.10 for additional details.

Overall rationale for the amendment: add new AESI of 'malnutrition and inadequate fluid intake' and update the title and text for AESI of 'ketoacidosis due to inadequate nutritional intake and other types of metabolic acidosis and ketosis'; provide more detailed guidance on recommending, monitoring, and managing nutritional intake and hydration; update criteria for dose modification; and include adjudication of urgent visit for heart failure.
Added a note in Inclusion Criterion 8 to address the usage of gender-neutral terms (AMAB and AFAB) in the document. For clarification and consistency with TRANSCEND T2D protocols.
Removed the word 'clinically significant' from Exclusion Criterion 22. Clarification to avoid ambiguity.
Defined study intervention in Exclusion Criterion 36 as retatrutide, placebo, or an active comparator. Clarification.
Updated calcitonin units from 'ng/L' to 'pg/mL (Conventional) and pmol/L (SI)' in Exclusion Criterion 24 and in Section 8.3.3.8. To align with central lab reporting.
Added the word 'in a blinded fashion' for all dose adjustments managed through IWRS. Clarification.

Updated the section title from 'Meals and Dietary Restrictions' to 'Meals and Nutrition'. Added more detailed guidance on monitoring and managing nutritional and hydration status throughout the study.
Added recommendation for monitoring weight after dose reduction for BMI ≤20 kg/m2. To provide additional guidance regarding the management of participants with BMI ≤20 kg/m2.
Additional note added to clarify the intended purpose of each estimand. Added a clarification to the definition of 'population' for treatment regimen and efficacy estimand attributes.
